normative_extracts.quote: With the u or v flag enabled, patterns match full Unicode code points and support Unicode property escapes.

browser_support.notes: UTF-16 RegExp + /u is universal; /v (unicodeSets) reached Baseline Newly/Widely in 2023-2024.

pipeline_phases: Irregexp Bytecode / Native Machine Code Compilation
UTF-16 Code Unit vs Code Point (/u, /v) Decoding
engine_internals.mechanism_summary: JS RegExp engines use backtracking NFA execution; nested quantifiers like (a+)+ trigger exponential O(2^n) backtracking on non-matching suffixes.

production_failures.symptom: Main thread freezes for 30+ seconds (ReDoS) on malformed email or URL input
production_failures.root_cause: Nested ambiguous quantifiers like /^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)*$/ cause O(2^n) backtracking in V8's Irregexp engine when a trailing character fails to match.
production_failures.mitigation: Eliminate nested quantifiers, use atomic/possessive-like patterns, or validate length before executing RegExp.

production_failures.symptom: Emoji or accented characters split in half or fail character-class matching
production_failures.root_cause: Without the /u or /v flag, RegExp operates on 16-bit UTF-16 code units, splitting surrogate pairs (e.g., emoji).
production_failures.mitigation: Always add the /u or /v flag when matching user text, emoji, or Unicode properties (\p{L}).
